svg.title: Cutting the corner increases the turning radius
svg.desc: Top view of a left turn. Path 2 follows the road bend. Path 1 starts wide, passes close to the inside edge at the apex, and exits wide. The corner-cutting arc has a larger radius than Path 2, allowing a greater speed for the same available friction. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Doubling the turning radius halves the required force at the same speed
Blue: r = 30 m; red: r = 60 m
Two 1000 kg cars at 12 m/s over the same 12 s. Radii and force arrows use common scales. The larger
circle turns through fewer radians; an available tire force must meet the requirement.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
